steps.text: Port Amble wakes up in August like someone who slept through three alarms and is now pretending they meant to.
Bunting zigzags between the lampposts. Gulls fight over a dropped pasty. A brass band is tuning up and hasn't agreed what key the morning is in.
Under a banner reading THE LONG WAY ROUND — NINE DAYS · SEVEN ISLANDS · ONE PASSPORT, forty-odd cyclists mill about in Lycra and nerves.
One of them isn't milling. She stands still in the middle of it, and everyone else has to walk round her.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Right.
The hat is purple and wide-brimmed, with a magenta feather that has views on the sea breeze.
It's tied under her chin with a ribbon. She lost it twice on the ride down. She won't lose it a third time in front of witnesses.
Under it: a striped face, long curly black-and-white hair pulled over one shoulder, purple lipstick put on at six a.m. like armour.
Purple linen shirt, sleeves rolled. Her purple coat is folded in her pannier. Even in August, she couldn't leave it behind.
The stillness isn't confidence. It's someone holding something heavy, very carefully. Nobody looks that closely. She makes sure of it.
Against her hip leans a silver road bike, tuned and oiled by her own hands at two in the morning.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Nine days. Seven islands. Forty teams. One prize.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: And one rule I didn't read properly.
She takes the entry form out of her back pocket for the fourth time. The line is still there, in a cheerful curly font.
*All competitors ride in pairs. Partners are assigned by draw at registration. The draw is final. The draw is ALWAYS final. — P.*

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Who underlines "always" in a legal document.
Behind her, something tall says "Mind your head" to a lamppost. Then, after a pause, to her.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Sorry. Habit.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: I say it to everything shorter than me. Which is everything.
A giraffe: two metres of spots and patience, curly brown hair between his ossicones, and an olive-green coat he refuses to let the heat bully him out of.
Green eyes, unhurried. A box of paper cups held against his chest.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: You're a competitor. You've got the face.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: What face.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: The one where you've done all the maths and none of the breakfast. Lemonade?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: No.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: That's fine. I'll ask again at the windmill.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: I'm Giraffy. Checkpoints, campsite dinners, first aid. People navigate by me. "Left at the giraffe."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Zizzy.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Zizzy. Good. Have you got a partner yet?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I'm about to be given one. Apparently.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Ah. The Hat.
He says it the way people say "the weather". You don't argue with it. You dress for it.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: It's never been cruel. It's been strange.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Strange usually turns out alright. By about day five.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I don't have until day five.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Everybody does. That's how days work.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Good luck, Zizzy. Drink something.
The registration tent is striped red and white, like a circus that's lost its nerve. It's hotter inside than out.
At a trestle table of clipboards, rubber stamps and tiny blue passports, every stack squared to the edge, sits the organiser.
Pia. Neat black bob, small round ears, enormous round wire glasses, plum cardigan buttoned to the throat. It is twenty-nine degrees.
She looks up, sees the hat, and briefly considers hiding under the table.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Oh — hello. Entry? Sorry. Yes. Name?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Zizzy. Entry forty-one. I'd like to request an exemption.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: No.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You haven't heard it.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: It's — it's always the same one. "May I ride alone." Every year.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: I wrote the answer down so I wouldn't have to say it.
She slides over a laminated card, in bold looping handwriting much louder than she is: *NO. The Long Way Round is not about being good alone. It is about the other thing. — P.*

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: What other thing.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: The one you don't know yet. Passport.
A tiny blue booklet. Embossed in gold on the cover: a bicycle, a compass, and seven dots in a curve like a necklace.

She doesn't recite the rules. She slides a second laminated card across and taps each line as Zizzy reads it: stamps, riddles, ferries, the tidal causeway, booked campsites, first pair across the line at Lastlight with a full passport.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Tents are — two-person. Sorry. Pairs share.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Both riders. Crossing together. That's — the important one.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: And the prize is still —

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Eight thousand. Split two ways.
Four thousand. She has done the sum so often it's worn a groove.
Four thousand covers three months' back rent on an old hardware shop in her home town, the shelves long gone.
A sprung wooden floor. A rack of old foils. Her grandmother's little flat upstairs. A sign out front, still in her grandmother's handwriting.
The lease runs out on the fifteenth of September. She hasn't told anyone. Telling people gets you the face.
Under the hat and the lipstick and the plan there's a quiet grey place she visits more than she'd admit. The floor is empty there, and nobody is teaching on it.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: You went somewhere just then.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Calculating ferry times.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Okay. Draw's at ten. Please don't try to swap.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Someone tried a lemon drizzle cake last year.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Did it work?

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: I ate the cake. It didn't work.
Ten o'clock. The band has settled on a key, a brave one. A crowd stands in a horseshoe round a little wooden stage.
On a stool on the stage sits the Hat: a battered black top hat full of folded slips.
Zizzy takes the edge of the crowd, where she can see everyone and nobody can see her look nervous.
Someone got there first. He's leaning on the railing, hands in the pocket of a rust-orange hoodie, despite the heat.
A fox, shaggy copper-red hair over his eyes. He looks at her bike first. Then her tyres. Then her shoes. Then her face. Like he's reading the specs.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Good tyres.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I know.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Yeah. You would.
That's all. He goes back to watching the stage.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Do I know you?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Fenn. I've done this a few times.
A rabbit bounces up beside him holding three ice lollies: wavy blonde hair, long ears up, an olive trench coat tied round her waist by the sleeves.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: "A few times." He's won it twice. There's a plaque in the ferry office. He walks past it with his eyes shut.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Hi! I'm Clover. Lolly? I always buy one for whoever's standing next to Fenn. He won't talk to them.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Thank you.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: You're welcome. I love your hat.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I'm going to try very hard to beat you, and I'll feel bad about it, and then I'll buy you another lolly.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're partners already? I thought the draw was random.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: It is! The Hat's put us together three years running. Pia says it's fate.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I think the Hat just likes him. Everybody does, eventually. It takes about a week.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Ten days.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: See? He's warming up already.
On stage, Pia approaches the microphone the way you'd approach a large dog. She taps it. It squeals. Half the gulls leave.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Um. Good morning. Wayfarers.
A cheer, louder than she was ready for. She flinches, pushes her glasses up, and unfolds a card.
Then she reads. The words on the card are bolder than she is, and she leans on them like a railing.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: "Welcome to the nineteenth Long Way Round. Some of you came to win. Some of you came for the view. Some of you lost a bet.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: All of you will finish knowing one person better than you meant to. That isn't a promise. It's a warning."
Laughter. Pia goes pink and folds the card very small. Zizzy doesn't laugh. Her arms are folded so tight she can feel her own heartbeat.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: When I call your number, please take a slip. The name is your partner. No swapping. Thank you. Sorry. Thank you.
The draw takes forever. Strangers pair off, grinning awkwardly. Two old badgers, clearly married, draw each other and act shocked.
Fenn draws Clover. The crowd groans fondly. Clover throws both arms in the air like she's won something, and Fenn lets her.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Forty-one?
Zizzy walks up. The boards creak. The Hat is warmer than it ought to be, as if it's been sitting in the sun thinking about her.
She takes a slip. Unfolds it. Reads it.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …"Pony."

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Um. Pony? Is there a — Pony?
Silence. Then, from the back, a clatter, an apology, a second clatter, and a waving hand.
A horse. Cream-tan fur, tan ears, messy blond hair escaping from under something dark her brain refuses to process yet. Round wire glasses, pushed up as he waves.
A mustard shirt. A wooden practice sword strapped across his back. A yellow scarf knotted round a set of handlebars like a flag.
The handlebars belong to two bicycles that have made a long-term commitment.
A tandem. A rented, mint-green tandem, with a wicker basket on the front and a bell shaped like a duck.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Hi! That's — me. I'm Pony. Hello.
Forty cyclists turn to see what Zizzy does next.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Is that a tandem.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It — yes. The single bikes at the rental place were gone.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: They said a tandem was "two bikes for the price of one". Which, now I say it out loud, isn't how maths works.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Is that a duck.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's a bell. It quacks. I didn't choose it. I've grown fond of it.
To the left, Clover makes a delighted little noise. And Fenn, hands in pockets, says quietly — but the quay has gone quiet too —

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Huh. Good year.

steps.prompt: How does Zizzy take the draw?

options.label: "Fine. Keep up."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Fine.
She steps off the stage, walks straight through the crowd and stops in front of him.
He's a centimetre taller. With the hat, she has twelve on him, and she makes sure he can tell.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Here's how this goes. I ride in front. I steer. I set the pace. You pedal, and you don't talk on the climbs.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We win. Then we never see each other again.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's… a very complete plan.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Keep up.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'll try. Just so you know, I've never been good at "keeping up".

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm more of a "catching up later" person.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Then catch up faster.
She walks off. He watches her go, then looks down at the duck bell.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: She likes us. I can tell.

options.label: "...Why did you enter?"

steps.text: She has three cutting things ready.
But he's holding that ridiculous green tandem as if it might wander off, and his ears are pinned flat with nerves, and a question comes out instead.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Why did you enter?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Oh. Um.
He pushes his glasses up. They didn't need pushing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I wanted to finish something.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Finish what?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Anything, really. I've had a year of starting things.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: This has an actual finish line. With a banner. Hard to miss.
Not the answer of someone here to win. Not an answer she can use. She files it away somewhere careful anyway.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I'm here to win.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Then between us we've got the whole thing covered.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: That isn't how it works.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's how it works on a tandem. One steers. One — also pedals.

options.label: Turn to Pia: "I'd like to discuss a swap."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Pia. A word.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Oh. Um. No?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: He's brought a tandem. With a basket. You can't expect me to win a nine-day race on a bicycle that quacks.
Pia, wordlessly, holds up the laminated card. *NO.* It was laminated for exactly this.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: That's a card.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: It's a very good card.
The crowd laughs. Too late, Zizzy realises the whole quay heard her.
At the back, the horse holds his tandem a little tighter, smiling the way people smile at a party when they've overheard someone ask who invited them.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's fine. I'd want to swap me too.
He says it lightly. It isn't light. Something in her chest gives an irritating twist, like stepping on a stair that isn't there.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …I didn't mean you. I meant the duck.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: The duck's very hurt.
The draw finishes. Strangers stand in pairs with the bright, terrified politeness of a first day at school.
Her silver road bike leans against a bollard, abandoned and beautiful.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You can bring your bike. If you want. We could ride separately.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: The rules say "same bike or two bikes".

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Two bicycles means two punctures. Two sets of brakes. Two people choosing their own line on a descent.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: And one tandem means…

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: One person choosing. Me.
She looks at the tandem like a general looking at a battlefield she didn't pick.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Tandems are faster on the flat. Two engines, one wind resistance. Saltmere is mostly flat.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's a better racing machine. If both riders are any good.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Define "any good."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Have you ridden one before?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Yes.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Recently?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Once. At the seaside, when I was eight. My uncle steered. We hit a candyfloss stall.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It wasn't my fault, but I was the one covered in candyfloss, so in the eyes of the law…

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Okay.
She takes her silver bike to the support van: sky blue, battered, a bumper sticker reading I BRAKE FOR GOSSIP.
Leaning on it is a guy with very dark messy hair, dark pointed ears that could be cat or wolf depending on his mood, and a navy jacket with a tan collar, sleeves shoved up over greasy forearms.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Ooh. Gorgeous. Not you. The bike.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Well. Also you. But I'm working.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Can you get it to the finish.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Not a scratch. I'll talk to her every night. Tell her you miss her.
He glances past her at the mint-green tandem. His eyebrows climb.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: No. You're riding *that*? With *him*?

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Oh, this is going to be the best nine days of my life.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Apparently.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Bruno. Van, ferries, spanners and unsolicited commentary.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: If it breaks, find me. If he breaks, also find me. I'll want to watch.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're very helpful.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: I really am.
The test lap is the quay and back. Pia insists every team does one, "so we can identify the disasters early and arrange for an ambulance."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Front. Me.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Back. Me. Got it. Do I hold on to anything?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: There are handlebars back here, but they don't turn. Emotional-support handlebars.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The stoker doesn't steer. The stoker pedals, balances, and shouts if anything's coming from behind.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "Stoker"! Like a steam train. I'm the furnace.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Get on.
Getting on takes three attempts. One ends with Pony's wooden sword hitting Zizzy in the back of the head.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Why do you have a sword.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's a practice sword. It's wooden.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I always have it. It's a long story.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Is it a long story that ends with you taking it off?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: No.
It's the first thing he's said all morning without a nervous laugh on the end.
He shifts the sword to hang along his side, out of her way. That's the compromise. She lets it go. For now.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: On three, push off. One —

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Is it on three, or after three?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: On.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: So "one, two, go," or "one, two, three, go"?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: One. Two. Three.
They push off on different numbers.
The tandem lurches, wobbles, recovers, swings wide towards the crowd — and for one golden second it is actually riding. The chain hums. The quay slides past. The feather lifts —

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Is that a giraffe —
— and then it isn't. The front wheel catches a trailing string of bunting.
The bunting is attached to Giraffy. Giraffy is attached to a ladder, hanging more bunting.
A long, slow, almost graceful collapse. Flags. Wheels. A ladder. A giraffe. From somewhere underneath, the duck bell quacks once, faintly.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: I'm alright. I'm decorated. But I'm alright.
Zizzy lies on the warm cobbles with a pennant across her face. If she doesn't move, the ground might kindly open up.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Are you hurt?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: My pride is dead. Leave it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I can't, I'm tangled with it.
Then a sound escapes her. Short, sharp, quickly strangled. If anyone asked, she'd call it a cough.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Did you just laugh?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: No.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You did. You laughed. I heard it. It was like a door creaking.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Say one more word and I'll tie you to the back of this bike with the bunting.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's six words. I counted.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Also, I'm already tied to the bike with the bunting.
A shadow falls across her. Fenn, hands in pockets, looking down at the wreck. His expression is hard to read.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You leaned late.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I'm aware.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Stoker didn't know you were leaning. That's all it is.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Tandems are mostly talking.
He holds a hand down — not to her, to Pony — and pulls him and the bunting upright in one easy motion. Then he walks off, as if he hadn't said anything useful at all.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Are you okay? You were amazing. I mean, terrible, but amazing.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: You've got a flag in your hair. Two flags.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Leave them. I live here now.
Pia hovers at the edge of the wreckage, clipboard to her chest, eyes huge behind her glasses. She speaks mostly to the clipboard.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: The last pair who crashed into Giraffy was nine years ago.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: They got married.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Don't.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Sorry. History. Sorry.
Twenty minutes later Bruno has straightened the mudguard, reset the chain and pulled bunting out of the gears, in four words. Two of them were "hold" and "this".
Zizzy sits in the van's open side door, holding a cold lemonade can to the elbow she skinned on the cobbles. Pony checks the wicker basket for damage like it's a wounded pet.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: The basket's fine.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Thank goodness.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You laugh, but it's going to carry the snacks.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: The basket's the most important member of the team.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I've known you an hour and you've already prioritised a basket over me.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: No — I just meant — you're obviously the most important.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: As a captain. Of the bike. A professional assessment.
He's blushing. Even through cream-tan fur, the pink climbs his muzzle to the tan ears poking out from under — Zizzy blinks — a black knit beanie. In August.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Are you wearing a wool hat.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's a beanie. It's not wool, it's — it's a wool blend.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's twenty-nine degrees.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You're wearing a hat.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Mine has a brim. It's for shade. Yours is for — what is yours for.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Comfort. It's — it's a comfort hat.
His mustard shirt is buttoned wrong by one. She decides not to fight a war on three fronts.
Bruno slides out from under the tandem on a wheeled board, wiping his hands.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Chain was off. Front brake was rubbing. There's bunting in places bunting shouldn't go.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: I've done things for this bike today I'll never speak of.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Was the brake rubbing before the crash?

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Oh, for *ages*.
She turns slowly to Pony.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: The rental place said the squeal was "character."

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: It had character. Now it has brakes. You're welcome.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Also, Pony, mate — the beanie. Bold. I respect it. You're going to die.
He hands Zizzy a brass pump, a puncture kit and a laminated card with his number.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Call if you're stuck. Any island, any hour. Ferries wait for nobody, so I wait for everybody.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Don't tell anyone. It ruins my image.
Then he's off, whistling, shouldering spare wheels. Pony watches him go with something like awe.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: He's like a lighthouse. A rude lighthouse. With a wrench.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You like lighthouses.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I like most things that stand in one place and help people. It's a good job for a building.
She doesn't answer. She thinks of a sign over an old hardware shop, in her grandmother's handwriting. Standing in one place, helping people, for fifty years.
She puts the thought back where it came from.

Eleven o'clock. The start line is a chalk stripe across the cobbles. Forty-odd teams on bikes, tandems and, in one alarming case, a recumbent trike. The band plays something triumphant, slightly out of tune.
Pia comes to the microphone one last time.
She holds up a laminated card: FIRST RIDDLE INSIDE FRONT COVER · FIRST CHECKPOINT ON BRACKENHOLM · STAMP BY SUNSET OR LOSE AN HOUR.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Um. Good luck. Sorry.
Zizzy flips the passport open. In Pia's curly handwriting:
*"I turn my back to the wind but never leave my hill. I grind, but I'm not angry. I wave, but I'm not friendly. Find me where the heather sings."*

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: "Heather" means Brackenholm. The heath. We'll know it when we see it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's a windmill.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "Grinds but isn't angry": a millstone. "Waves but isn't friendly": the sails.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "Turns its back to the wind" is a trick line. A tower mill only turns its cap.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: There's one on the north side of Brackenholm. Built 1803. It's on the poster in the ferry office. Behind the plaque that says Fenn won twice.
Zizzy stares at him.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You read the posters in the ferry office.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I read everything. Leaflets, plaques, the backs of shampoo bottles. It's a condition.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …That's useful.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Was that a compliment?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It was an observation.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'll take an observation.
Two places down, Fenn and Clover are clipped in. Clover waves with her whole arm. Fenn gives Pony the smallest nod. One navigator to another.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Tower mill. North side.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You heard?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You think out loud.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Fenn! We're meant to be rivals!

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: They already had it.
Clover rolls her eyes fondly, then catches Zizzy's gaze, rider to rider, and smiles. Not a challenge. An invitation to one.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: See you at the windmill. Ride fast.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I want it to be a proper race.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It will be.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Good!
Pia climbs onto a crate with a starting pistol that fires only confetti, looks at the crowd, panics slightly, and holds up a card: *ON YOUR MARKS.*
Zizzy grips the bars. Behind her, the tandem shifts as Pony settles his weight, and for the first time it's level. As if the bike is holding its breath for both of them.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Zizzy?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: What.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: On three or after three?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: On. Go.
The confetti pistol pops. The crowd roars. Forty teams lunge forward.
And the mint-green tandem — quacking bell, wooden sword, a captain who refuses to laugh — rolls off the line perfectly straight. And keeps going.
Behind them, Giraffy is still waving from under the bunting.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Go on, forty-one. Steady does it.
The ferry to Brackenholm is a squat white boat called the *Persistence*. Pony points out that this is either very inspiring or a warning.
Forty teams cram onto the car deck, bikes wedged together like cutlery in a drawer. The tandem takes up two spaces. A heron on a buoy watches with open disapproval.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Did you know Brackenholm means "the island of bracken"? "Holm" is an old word for a small island.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: So it's basically called Fern Island. Which is lovely. Unless you're allergic to ferns.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Are you allergic to ferns?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I don't think so. I've never been tested. I've never had a reason.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Then don't start now.
She has the race map folded into a tight square and traces the route with one claw. Coast road north, then inland across the heath to the windmill. Eleven miles.
Flat, mostly. One hill the map calls Gallows Rise, which she chooses not to find ominous.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You're going the coast road?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's the fastest.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's the longest.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's paved. The heath tracks are sand. Sand eats tyres.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Fast is about surface, not distance.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Huh. Okay. That's actually — good.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I know.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You say "I know" a lot.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I know a lot.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Okay, that one was funny.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You're allowed to admit that one was funny.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It wasn't a joke.
It was a joke. The feather gives her away, twitching in the breeze in a way that looks, if you squint, like a wink.
Brackenholm, it turns out, is not mostly flat.
It's a long, low purple wave of an island, heather to the horizon, a single white road threaded through it like a stitch.
The first mile goes well. The second mile goes less well.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Shift up.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Up as in the bigger number or up as in harder?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Same thing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It isn't, though, on this bike. The gear numbers go backwards. The rental man said so.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: He also said "she pulls a bit to the left, but so does my wife," which wasn't the information I needed.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Harder. Shift harder.
He shifts. The chain clunks. Their legs fall out of sync, the pedals bumping like two people trying to get through the same doorway.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're fighting me.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm — not fighting — I'm following — you keep changing —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I'm not changing. I'm steady. Match me.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I can't see you! I can see your back. And your hat.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Mainly the hat. The hat is a very large percentage of my view.
Half a mile of silence. The chain, the wind, and a skylark overhead that seems to be laughing at them.
Two weasels blow past on matching road bikes. One rings a bell. It doesn't quack.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Weasel
steps.text: Nice duck!

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We're being overtaken by weasels.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Technically they're stoats. The tips of their tails are black —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Pony.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Weasels. Absolutely weasels.
They stop at a crossroads, mostly because Zizzy is about to say something she'd have to apologise for. She doesn't apologise.
A wooden signpost leans like it's tired of giving directions. One arm says WINDMILL 4. One says GALLOWS RISE.
The third has been bleached by the sun into philosophical blankness.
Pony climbs off, sits in the heather and pours his water bottle over his own head.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Better.
The water runs off his beanie, which stays on. It may actually be steaming.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Take the hat off.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's fine. It's practically a cooling system now. Evaporation. Science.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're going to get heatstroke in a wool hat on a heath in August.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Wool *blend*.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We're behind.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: We're fine. It's day one. Nobody wins a nine-day race on day one.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: People lose them on day one.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Can I say something? You can tell me I'm wrong after.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: But you have to let me finish first. That's the rule.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Whose rule.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Mine. I just made it. It's new. It's very fresh.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Go on.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: When you speed up, you don't tell me. You just go. I feel it a second later, so I push harder to catch up.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Then you feel me pushing and think I'm fighting you. I'm not. I'm late. I'm always a second late, because I'm at the back.
She opens her mouth to say that isn't how it works. Then closes it, because it's exactly how it works.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: So maybe you say "up" before you go up. And "easy" before you ease off.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Then I'm not late. I'm just — with you.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: That's a lot of talking.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You hate talking.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I hate unnecessary talking.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: This would be necessary talking. Your favourite kind.
She looks at the horizon. A kestrel hangs over the heather, perfectly still against the wind, holding its place without effort.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Fine. "Up." "Easy." "Stop." "Bump."

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: And "duck."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: For what.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Low branches. Or if I want to ring the bell.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Fine.
It works. Annoyingly, ridiculously well.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Up.
They shift together. The chain sings. The tandem leaps forward like it's been waiting all day for someone to ask nicely.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Bump.
A pothole flashes under them. They lift out of the saddle at the same moment and settle again, as if they'd rehearsed it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That was beautiful.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It was a pothole.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It was a beautiful pothole.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Easy. Corner.
They lean into the bend together. Heather blurs purple on both sides. After the corner the wind is at their backs, and they're flying.
Up ahead, the weasels. Or stoats.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Up.
They pass them on a slight downhill, humming like a train. Pony leans out and rings the bell. It quacks, triumphantly.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: NICE BELL!
Zizzy doesn't look round. But under the hat, the corner of her mouth has gone up. And stays there.
The windmill stands on a rise in the middle of the heath: a tall white tower, four lattice sails turning slowly. A crooked smiling sun is painted on its cap.
Giraffy is already there. Nobody knows how. He's folded into a camp chair under a parasol, coat on, with a cashbox, an ink pad and a rubber stamp lined up on a crate.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Forty-one. Both of you. Both wheels. Good.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Stamp.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Stamp. There. A windmill. I carved it out of a potato last night.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Pia thinks it's professional. I haven't corrected her. It makes her happy.
One inky windmill in the blue passport, slightly lopsided. Zizzy looks at it longer than she needs to. It's the first one.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Riddle's on the door. Pia says riddles should be found, not handed over.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: She's very firm about it. On paper.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: And in person?

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: In person, she asked me to nail it up. She was worried she'd do it crooked.
On the green door, a sheet of parchment curls slightly in the heat.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "Second riddle. *Where the road gives up and the rock goes on, where the dark is kept and the light is gone — no, the light is SHOWN — climb to the keeper, who never sleeps, and ask her the hour the ocean keeps.*"
He reads it with his head tilted, the way some people listen to music, lips moving over the lines.
Zizzy retightens her hat ribbon so she has an excuse to watch him think.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Well?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "The road gives up and the rock goes on." Cliffs. "The keeper who never sleeps", "the light is shown": a lighthouse.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Gullrock has a lighthouse. But that's island three. We should be going to island two's checkpoint first. So that doesn't —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: There isn't a checkpoint on the second island in the schedule.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Brackenholm is days one and two. Tomorrow's a loop round the island and back to camp.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The race goes Brackenholm, then Gullrock. The first island takes two days. There's no second checkpoint to find.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Then it's Gullrock lighthouse. "Ask her the hour the ocean keeps": the tide table.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Lighthouses post tide tables. It wants us there at a certain tide.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Or.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Or?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: "Where the dark is kept." That's not a lighthouse. That's a cave. Or a quarry.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: There's an old chalk quarry on the south side. The quarry road's a dead end. "The road gives up."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It might be a trick. Pia likes tricks. You said so about the windmill.
They look at each other. The sails creak round. Across the heath, two more teams are pedalling for the hill.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm pretty sure it's the lighthouse. But you're the captain.
He says it plainly. No sulking. He hands it to her and waits.

options.label: Trust Pony: the lighthouse, ride for the evening ferry to Gullrock.

steps.text: She reads it again. "The light is shown." The dark isn't kept *in*. It's kept *out*.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Lighthouse.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Really?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You read the ferry office posters. I read the map.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: On a map, the quarry's a dead end. In a riddle, it's the trap.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: So you trust me.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I trust the poster.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's basically me with extra steps.
Giraffy has been listening the way a hill listens to weather. He holds out a paper cup.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Lemonade. Told you I'd ask again at the windmill.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Fine.
It's very good lemonade. She isn't telling him that either.
Giraffy's ferry list says *Monday: Gullrock, 7:40 a.m.* Tomorrow's loop, they'll ride knowing where they're headed. On a nine-day race, that's half the battle.

options.label: Trust her instinct: check the chalk quarry first.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Quarry. We check it. It's on the way back to camp anyway.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's a bit off the way back to camp.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's a bit on the way.
It isn't. It's six miles south on a road the map calls "unimproved", which turns out to mean sand with ambitions.
The quarry is a white bowl cut into the hillside, hot and empty except for a sheep who looks at them like they've interrupted something private.
No checkpoint. No parchment. Just a rusty sign — DANGER — DEEP WATER — NO SWIMMING — and under it, in marker: OR RIDDLES.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Pia.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It was a very good guess.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It was a wrong guess.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Those aren't opposites.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I've done loads of good wrong guesses. I'm basically made of them.
She waits for "I told you so." It doesn't come. He takes a photo of the sign and grins.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: For the memoirs. "Chapter One: The Quarry. A Lesson in Humility, Mostly for Sheep."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Next time I'll listen.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Did you just —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: No. Get on the bike.
They lose the light, an hour, and her last scrap of patience on the sand road back to camp.
But he didn't say it. She keeps remembering that.
The campsite is a field at the edge of the heath, sloping to the sea. Little tents in neat rows. A long trestle table.
Strings of bulbs between poles flicker on as the sun goes down orange behind the dunes.
Across the whole field drifts a smell of rosemary and onion and something slowly simmering. It makes you forget your legs.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Stew. Lentil and tomato. There's a secret ingredient.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: It's patience. And more lentils.
They arrive the way everyone arrives on day one: stiff, salty, walking as if they've just been issued legs and haven't read the manual.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I can't feel my — anything. Is that normal?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Saddle. You'll feel it tomorrow.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You say that like a threat.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's a forecast.
Bruno pre-pitches the tents. Nobody has seen him sleep. Each has a number on a little flag. Forty-one is the smallest, last in the row, by the hedge.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's one tent.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's a two-person tent.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It looks like a one-and-a-half-person tent.
Bruno strolls past with a mallet on his shoulder, sees their faces, and stops, delighted.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Oh, have we met the tent? Isn't she cosy?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Are there any spares?

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: There's the van.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I'll take the van.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: I sleep in the van. You're welcome to join me, but I snore and I talk about carburettors.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: No? Pairs share, sunshine. Rules. Pia laminated them.
He keeps walking.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'll sleep outside. I like outside. Stars. Fresh air.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Hedgehogs, probably. I can make friends with a hedgehog.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Don't be stupid. It's a tent. It's got a divider.
It does have a divider: a thin nylon flap that zips down the middle. She has never been so grateful for a strip of fabric.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Left side's mine. Right side's yours. The divider stays zipped. That's the rule.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Whose rule?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Mine. It's new. It's very fresh.
He laughs — a real laugh, startled out of him, bright as the bell — and she turns away so he won't see her face.
Dinner is at the long table, forty teams shoulder to shoulder, all talking at once about the windmill and the wind and who fell off where.
Giraffy ladles stew slowly and evenly, the same for everyone, as if fairness could be measured with a ladle. Pony gets one extra spoonful.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: For the bunting. No hard feelings. It's had worse days.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You're a good person, Giraffy.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: I'm a tall person. From down there, people mix the two up.
Fenn and Clover sit opposite, because Clover waves them over before anyone can choose otherwise. Fenn eats with his hood half up. Clover has saved them bread.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: You made it! I was watching the hill for you.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Did you get the windmill? Fenn said you would.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: I said probably.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: He said "probably" in a way that meant yes.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I speak Fenn. It's mostly shrugs.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: How far ahead were you?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Forty minutes.
Not a boast. Just a number, put on the table like salt. Somehow that's worse.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Sorry. He's been doing this for years. He knows where the wind turns.
Under the table, Pony nudges her elbow with his. A small bump, like the tandem going over a crack in the road.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Up?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You've got the "up" face. He's not even doing anything.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm just telling you before you go.
She stares at him. Then, deliberately, she drops her shoulders, picks up her spoon, and turns back to Fenn.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Forty minutes. It'll look lovely on the plaque.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Doesn't matter on day one.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Then why say it?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You asked.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: He's not trying to wind you up. That's just his face.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I thought he hated me for a whole year. Turned out he was concentrating.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: I was concentrating.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: He fell off a pedalo once, though. In front of everyone.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: There was a jellyfish.
The table laughs. Zizzy realises she's laughing too. Just a little. Just the door-creak.
Beside her, Pony has stopped eating to watch it happen, like someone watching a rare bird land.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: What.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Nothing! Stew. Very good stew. Excellent lentils.
Later, the field is dark except for embers and tents lit from inside like paper lanterns.
Somebody plays a harmonica badly. Somebody else asks them, kindly, to stop.
Zizzy sits on a crate outside tent forty-one, oiling the chain by torchlight, link by link, the way her grandmother taught her to clean a foil blade: properly, or not at all.
Pony comes back from the tap with two mugs of tea and sits in the grass beside her. He doesn't say anything at first, which is new. He holds out a mug.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Thanks.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Giraffy made it. It's mostly sugar. He says it's for "morale."
They drink. The sea shushes beyond the dunes. Overhead, the sky is doing what it only does far from towns: showing off.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's Cygnus. The swan. The bright one's Deneb. About two thousand light years away.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: So that light left it before anyone on Earth had invented —
He stops himself. Glances at her.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Sorry. I'm doing it again. The plaque thing. You can tell me to stop.
She thinks about saying "Stop." It would be easy. It's what she'd normally say.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Before anyone had invented what?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Um. Bicycles. Chain stitching. Probably soup.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: People had soup.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Not good soup.
She snorts into her tea. She didn't mean to.
They sit. The chain's done. The tea goes cold. The stars wheel over. Neither of them hurries to go and face the tent.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Zizzy?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Mm.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Why do you want to win? I mean — everybody wants to win.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: But you want it the way people want air.
The question lands exactly where she's been guarding all day. She goes still, the way she goes still on the strip when an opponent finds the gap.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Money.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: For what?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Things.
He waits. She gives him nothing else. After a moment he nods, as if that's a reasonable answer. It isn't.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Okay.
Just that. He picks at the grass. The harmonica has finally stopped.
It's worse than if he'd pushed. Pushing she can parry.
She looks at the chain instead. Her grandmother oiled the blades on Sunday nights with the radio on low, humming off-key. Zizzy hasn't been able to stand that station since March.
She hasn't said that out loud to anyone. There's a lot she hasn't said. It sits in her like cold water at the bottom of a well, very still, very deep. Most days she walks round the edge of it.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Bed. Early start. Island loop tomorrow, then the Monday ferry.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Right. Divider zipped.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Divider zipped.
The tent is very small. The divider is very thin. Zizzy lies on her side in the dark, hat at her feet, listening to the sea and to Pony trying very hard to be quiet, and failing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Sorry. Sleeping bag. It's like getting into a fish.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Go to sleep.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Going.
Rustle. Rustle. Silence. Then, very quietly:

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Zizzy?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: What.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Today was good. The bit after the crossroads. When it worked.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That was really good.
She doesn't answer. The nylon glows faintly blue from a torch somebody's left on outside.
It was good. The best ten miles she's ridden in a year. She isn't going to tell him. She's going to roll over and sleep like a professional.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Up.
A pause. On the other side of the divider, a soft, delighted huff of breath.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Up.
Morning on Brackenholm arrives early and all at once, like a curtain yanked open. By six the tent glows orange. By half past, it's an oven.
Zizzy has been up since five, on the crate, race map across her knees, hat beside her, a mug of Giraffy's sugar tea going cold in the grass.
Today is the loop: forty miles clockwise round the island, a stamp at the beacon on Gallows Rise, back to this field by sunset.
No riddle. Distance, heat and wind. Pure racing. Her favourite kind.
Behind her, the tent unzips, and a horse falls out of it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You were right.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: About what.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: The saddle. The forecast. I've been sat on by the forecast.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Every part of me that touched that bike has filed a complaint.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It wears off by day four.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Day *four*?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Five.
He puts his face back in the grass. A hand gropes about until it finds the beanie and pulls it on. Only then does he sit up.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's going to be thirty-one degrees today.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Then I'll be the best-dressed person at thirty-one degrees.
Bruno wanders past with a bucket of tyre levers and toast in his mouth. He removes the toast to speak, which means he thinks it's worth it.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Morning, lovebirds. How was the tent? Did the divider hold?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Yes.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Shame. Pony, the beanie. You're committing. I admire it.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: I've put an ice pack in the van with your name on it. Literally. I wrote PONY'S FUNERAL on it in marker.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's actually really thoughtful.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: …It was meant to be mean.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's both. That's allowed.
Bruno opens his mouth, closes it, puts the toast back in, and walks off looking slightly defeated.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You just disarmed him.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Did I? I just said thank you.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Same thing, with some people.
The first fifteen miles are the best riding of Zizzy's life. She'll admit it later, under oath, possibly. Not now.
The road runs down the east coast, a grey ribbon between heather and sea, and the wind is behind them.
With "up" and "easy" and "bump", the tandem stops being two people fighting over a bicycle. It's one animal with four legs and a duck.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Up.
They shift. They fly. They pass three teams in a mile.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: We're good at this!

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We're adequate at this.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: We're adequate at this so fast!
The feather streams back. Pony has learned to tilt his head left to see past the brim.
If he watches her shoulders, he can feel her next move before she calls it.
He doesn't tell her. She'd find it suspicious.
Then the road turns inland at a lonely white farmhouse. The wind swings round and punches them in the face, and the heather closes in, a purple sea with no landmarks at all.
Two hours later, they're lost.
Properly, existentially lost. The kind where you start to wonder whether the map is of this island at all.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: This is the crossroads.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's *a* crossroads.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's *the* crossroads. The one with the blank sign.
She points. The signpost has three arms. One says GALLOWS RISE 3. One says FARM. The third has been bleached into nothing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Yesterday's crossroads had a sign for the windmill. This one doesn't.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Then the island has two crossroads with blank signs.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's — honestly, from what I've seen of Brackenholm, very possible.
The sun is directly overhead. There's been no shade since the farmhouse.
Her shirt is stuck to her back. Her lipstick has melted to a suggestion. Her bottle is empty.
Pony's beanie is, somehow, still on.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Take that thing off before you pass out and I have to carry you *and* the bike.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're red. You're red through your fur. Your nose is the colour of a postbox.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Is it?
It is. The tip of his muzzle has gone a shiny pink. He looks like a cartoon of a horse on holiday.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I put sunscreen on.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: When.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: …Last summer?
She closes her eyes. Counts to three in her grandmother's voice. *Un, deux, trois.* Before a bout, so nothing you do next is done in a temper.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We go to Gallows Rise. It's three miles. There's a stamp, and Giraffy, and water.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Then we work out where we went wrong.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Um. Which way is three miles?
They look at the signpost. GALLOWS RISE points, with great confidence, into a gorse bush.
Which is when they hear the bike.
A single quiet freewheel, ticking along a sandy track they hadn't noticed, half-hidden in the heather.
A rider in a rust-orange hoodie rolls out of nowhere and stops. One foot down. Hands on the bars.
Fenn. Alone.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Where's Clover?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Ahead. She's faster on the climbs. I'm faster on the sand. We swap.
He takes in the signpost, the gorse, the map in Zizzy's hand and Pony's nose in about two seconds. He says nothing. That's worse than laughing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Hi! We're lost.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We're not lost.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: We're *differently located*.
One corner of Fenn's mouth moves. It might be a smile. On him it's hard to tell.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Main road to the Rise goes back east, round the farm, then up the long way. Eight miles.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Eight.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.expr_raw: tilting his head at the sandy track
steps.text: Or this. Bridleway. Straight over the top. Two miles.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.expr_raw: tilting his head at the sandy track
steps.text: It's on the old map. The new one left it off.
He takes an old map from his hoodie pocket, soft, the creases gone white, and holds it open so they can see the thin dotted line through the heather.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: It's legal. Pia knows about it. She just doesn't put it on the new map.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Why not?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Says she likes people to find their own way. I think she forgot it was there.
Pony leans over her shoulder to look. Close enough that she can smell the sunburn on him, and the faint, absurd smell of wool.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's sand, though. You said sand eats tyres.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: It does.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Why are you telling us?
Fenn considers it, as if nobody has asked him before.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You're red. He's redder. It's thirty-one degrees.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Nobody wins anything on day two by watching someone pass out in a gorse bush.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: And it's more interesting if you're in it.
He folds the map. He doesn't offer it. He doesn't push. He waits, the way Pony waited at the windmill, which she finds unreasonably irritating in a rival.

options.label: "Show us the way." Take the bridleway.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Fine. Show us.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Follow my line. Stay off the soft bits. They're lighter coloured.
He sets off without another word. They follow.
The bridleway is narrow, sandy and lovely, a pale thread through heather so thick it hums with bees.
Fenn rides it like he's done it a hundred times, never more than a few lengths ahead.
The tandem rides it like a shopping trolley in a sandpit.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Bump. Bump. Soft — easy — easy —

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Which bit's soft? It's all — it's all sand-coloured —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The lighter sand.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's all the sand!

But they make it. Twenty minutes later the track tips over a crest, and there's Gallows Rise: a grassy hilltop, an old stone beacon, a parasol, a giraffe, and half the island laid out below like a quilt.
Fenn is already there, drinking. He nods when they roll up. Then he clips back in and goes down the far side after Clover.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Thank you.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Owe me one.
He says it lightly, and the wind takes it. But she hears it. She puts it somewhere she doesn't like to look.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Do you think he means it?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I think he means everything he says. That's the problem.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: He doesn't say much.

options.label: "We'll find our own way." Ride the long road.

steps.text: Zizzy looks at the old map. She looks at the bridleway. She looks at Pony's nose.
Then she thinks about stamping in at Gallows Rise because Fenn showed her how. About telling herself, later, she'd done it on her own.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We'll find our own way. Thank you.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Sure.
He doesn't seem to mind. He clips in and rides off up the sandy track, and in thirty seconds the heather has swallowed him.
Behind her, Pony lets out a long breath.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That was the right thing.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It was the slow thing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Those aren't opposites either.
She turns. He's pushing his glasses up his very pink nose. He isn't making a point. He just believes it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I don't like shortcuts. Even legal ones. It feels like borrowing something and not giving it back.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: And I've had a lot of those this year.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: A lot of shortcuts?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: A lot of things I didn't give back.
He doesn't explain. She doesn't ask. But for the first time she sees it in him too: a well. She'd assumed she was the only one with one.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Eight miles. Get on.
The long road is long, and hot. It goes round the farm twice, by her count, and ends in a hill so steep they both have to get off and push.
But at the top, with the beacon and the parasol and the giraffe and the island spread out below, Pony turns to her, face shining, and says —

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: We found it. We *found* it.
— and she's smiling. Really smiling, out in the open, hat pushed back. She doesn't stop straight away.

Gallows Rise, despite the name, is cheerful. A stone beacon. A bench with a brass plaque: *For Agnes, who always took the long way.* And Giraffy, under a parasol, with a cool box of water bottles packed in ice.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Drink first. Stamp second.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Stamp —

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Drink first.
She drinks. Half the bottle in one go. The rest goes over the back of her neck.
Giraffy turns to Pony. Looks at the beanie. The nose. The beanie again.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Pony.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I know.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Pony.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's a comfort hat!

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Comfort is good. Heatstroke is not comfortable. Take it off for ten minutes.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: It'll still be there after. Things you love usually are.
He says it so plainly that Pony does it. His blond hair springs up in a damp golden explosion, every strand pointing somewhere new.
Zizzy chokes on her water.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: What.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Nothing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's bad, isn't it.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's — architectural.
Giraffy stamps the passport — a little beacon with flames, carved into a potato — and hands it back.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Two stamps. Halfway round. Clover came through an hour ago. She asked if you were alright.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: She said, "Tell the hat I'm thinking about her."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …She said that?

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: She talks to everyone like that. It isn't a trick.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: It confused me for a whole summer too.
Four miles past the Rise, coasting down the long western slope with the wind behind them again and the afternoon going gold, the back tyre makes a noise like a sigh.
Then a hiss. Then a flubbing, thudding, deeply personal noise.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Was that us?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: That was us.
They roll to a stop. The back tyre is flat. In it, glinting innocently, is one long gorse thorn.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's the gorse bush. From the sign. I think it followed us.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's revenge.
Puncture kit from the basket. Bruno's brass pump. Tyre levers. She kneels on the verge and works with fast, practised fingers.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Can I help?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: No.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I could hold something.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You could stand there.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Okay.
He stands there for half a minute. Then he sits on the verge beside her, unwraps a squashed cheese sandwich, and holds half out to her without a word.
She ignores it. He keeps holding it. She ignores it harder. He keeps holding it.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Fine.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You're welcome.
Tyre off. Hole found. Sandpaper, glue, wait, patch: the speed and focus of someone defusing a bomb. Pony watches her hands.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You've done this a lot.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I fix things.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: What sort of things?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Bikes. Doors. Boilers. Floors.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Floors?
Her hands stop on the tyre. Floors. A sprung wooden floor with one board by the window that squeaks. She's re-screwed it four times since spring.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Pump.
He hands it over. She pumps the tyre up. Thirty seconds after it goes back on, it's flat again.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …There's a second thorn.
There are four thorns. There are three patches.
Twenty minutes later the sky-blue van trundles down the coast road, windows down, radio playing something with a lot of saxophone. It crunches to a stop beside them.

Bruno leans out, sunglasses on his head, and surveys the scene: dead tandem, empty puncture kit, Zizzy on the verge hugging her knees, Pony flat on his back in the grass with the beanie over his face.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Oh, no. Oh, *no*. Look at you both.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: You look like a painting called *Regret*.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Four thorns.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Gorse? Classic. Did you take the bridleway or did you take the gorse bush?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Does it matter?

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: To me? Hugely. For gossip.
He already has the back wheel off, though. He's quicker than she is, which she hates.
He turns the tube slowly by his ear, listening for the hiss, humming, and marks each hole with a stub of chalk.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: You did the first patch right, by the way. Good roughing. Clean glue.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Somebody taught you properly.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …My grandmother.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Ooh. A mechanic granny. Love that. Bet she was terrifying.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: She was a fencing teacher.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Was.
Just a word, put down on the road. Too late, Zizzy hears herself: "was".
He heard it too. He's the kind of person who hears everything and decides, every time, what to do with it.
He decides. He goes back to the tyre.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Well. You patch like someone who was taught to finish what they start.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: That's rarer than you'd think.
Behind them, under the beanie, Pony has gone very quiet.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: And as for you, sunshine. Sit up. I want to see the damage.
Pony sits up and takes the beanie off his face. Bruno sees the nose and makes a noise like a kettle starting to boil.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: You absolute *strawberry*. Didn't you put anything on?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Last summer.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: I love him. Can I keep him? I'll swap you for the van.
He digs a fat white tube of factor fifty out of a box in the back of the van and tosses it — not to Pony. To Zizzy.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Here. You do it. He can't see his own nose.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: He has hands.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.expr_raw: grinning, already turning back to the wheel
steps.text: And no mirror. Off you go.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.expr_raw: grinning, already turning back to the wheel
steps.text: I've got four thorns to deal with, and they're less trouble than you two.
There is a long silence on the verge.
Zizzy looks at the tube. Pony looks at the tube. A gull lands on the van roof and looks at the tube.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I can do it. Really. I'll just — I'll go by feel.
He squeezes far too much onto his palm and slaps it on his face. Most of it lands on his glasses.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: …That went well.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Give it to me.
She takes his glasses off first and wipes them on the hem of her shirt.
Without them his face looks younger, less sure of itself. His green eyes blink at her as if she's a blur he's trying to work out.
A small dab on the end of one finger. She leans in and touches it, very lightly, to the tip of his nose.
He goes completely still. Like the kestrel yesterday, holding its place in the wind.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Hold still.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I am holding still.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're holding your breath. It's not the same thing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's adjacent.
She works it in. Nose. The ridge of his muzzle. The tops of his cheeks, where the burn fades into cream-tan fur.
Her hand is perfectly steady. That matters, because nothing else about this is.
He's very close. Tiny freckles of darker tan at the base of his ears. A blush spreading under the white, which almost defeats the purpose.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're going red.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It's the sunburn.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's on top of the sunburn.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: …It's a layered sunburn.
Something happens to her mouth. She will not laugh. She presses her lips together and finishes his left cheek with military focus.
She sits back. Caps the tube. Puts his glasses back on with both hands, settling the wire arms over his ears.
Done. It has taken maybe forty seconds. It feels like considerably longer.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Done. Don't touch it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I won't touch it. I won't touch anything. I'm never touching anything again.
Behind the van, without looking up, Bruno starts whistling "Love Is in the Air".

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I will put a thorn in every tyre you own.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: No you won't. You like me.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I tolerate you.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: From you that's practically a proposal.
Four thorns take longer than one. Bruno waves them into the back of the van, "out of the sun, before you both turn into strawberries", and slams one door half shut for shade.
The back of the van is a nest: rope, a folded tarp, spare tyres, a crate of lemonade, a heap of old sleeping bags that smell of engine oil and, faintly, apples.
They sit on the sleeping bags, backs against the tyres. Shoulders not touching. Very deliberately not touching.
Saxophone from the cab radio, slow and lazy. Outside, tyre levers clinking and Bruno humming off-key. Heat ticks in the roof.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm just going to close my eyes. For one second.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Not sleeping. Resting my glasses.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You can't rest glasses.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: They've had a very long day.
Within a minute he's asleep, chin on his chest, beanie slipping over one eye.
Zizzy stays awake on principle. She watches the slice of sky through the door. She counts tyre levers by sound.
She's been up since five. She's ridden thirty miles, half of them into a headwind, and used every patch in the kit.
She'll close her eyes for one second. Not sleeping.
Twenty minutes later Bruno comes round to the back door, wiping his hands, and finds them both asleep.
Her head is on his shoulder, the purple hat squashed sideways against the tyres. His cheek rests on her curls. His nose has left a white smudge of sunscreen in her hair.
Bruno stands there. His mouth opens. A joke is loaded and ready.

then.text: He closes his mouth. Very quietly, he takes the PONY'S FUNERAL ice pack out of the cool box and lays it across their knees.
Then he goes back to the wheel and turns the radio down.

else.text: He takes out his phone and, very quietly, takes exactly one photo. For gossip. Then he looks at it, deletes it, swears under his breath, and turns the radio down.

steps.text: When they wake, ten minutes later, they're at opposite ends of the van, rubbing their necks, furious with nobody.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Good rest?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I didn't sleep.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Neither did I.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Course not.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Sunshine, you've got sunscreen in your hair. No idea how that happened.
Bruno sends them off with a new inner tube and a lecture about gorse, which is mostly an excuse to call Pony "strawberry" four more times.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Twelve miles back to camp. Sunset's at eight-forty.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: You'll make it if you don't do anything stupid.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We won't.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Oh, sunshine. You already have. You just haven't noticed yet.
He winks and drives off, saxophone fading down the coast road.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: What did he mean by that?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Nothing. He's a rude lighthouse. Get on.
They ride into the evening. The sea goes blue, then silver, then bronze. The wind pushes at their backs, kindly now, as if it's sorry about earlier.
For a long time neither of them says anything except "up," and "easy," and once, "bump."
Near the end, with the campsite lights coming on in the distance, Pony speaks. So quietly the wind almost takes it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Bruno said your grandmother "was."
Her hands tighten on the bars. Only slightly. He feels it anyway, through the frame.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Yes.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: March.
She doesn't know why she tells him the month. It just comes out, like air from a punctured tyre. A small sound you can't take back.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Was she the one who taught you to count?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You counted, at the crossroads. Under your breath. In French.
She's quiet so long he thinks he's overstepped. Then —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: *Un, deux, trois*. Before every bout. So nothing you do next is done in a temper.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: That's a good rule.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It was hers.
Something passes between them that isn't a word. Like the bump, when they both rise without being told.
He doesn't say anything else. But she feels him pedalling a little harder, taking a little more of the weight, without asking, all the way home.
At the campsite there's stew again. Giraffy says it's a different stew. It isn't.
Clover sits down beside Zizzy with a plate of bread and a tub of aloe vera gel.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: For his nose. Giraffy said. I always pack it.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Fenn burns too. He just won't admit it. He goes the colour of his hoodie and says it's "the light".

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Thank you.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: You're welcome! Did you find the Rise okay? Fenn said he saw you.
There's no trick in it. But down the table, Fenn glances up from his bowl. Just long enough to meet Zizzy's eyes.
Maybe he's thinking *you owe me one*. Maybe *you didn't need me*. With Fenn, you can't tell.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We found it.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I knew you would. Tomorrow's Gullrock! I've been looking forward to it all year.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: There's a cove where you can swim at night, and the water glows. Do you swim?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Yes.
Beside her, very quietly, Pony puts down his spoon.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Pony? Do you swim?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Oh, yes! Definitely. Loads. In the — the general sense.
Zizzy looks at him. He's suddenly very interested in his bread.
She files that away too, somewhere careful. Next to "a lot of things I didn't give back", and the comfort hat, and half a sandwich held out on a verge until she took it.
It's getting crowded in there. She's going to have to do something about it.
Not tonight. Tonight the divider stays zipped, and she lies in the dark listening to the sea, and to him on the other side of the blue nylon, trying very hard not to touch his nose.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Zizzy?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Don't touch it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I wasn't going to touch it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I was going to say goodnight.
A pause.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …Goodnight, Pony.
The 7:40 to Gullrock is smaller and older than the *Persistence*: a wooden boat called the *Mabel* that smells of diesel, rope and last year's fish.
The sea is flat and silver. Gulls ride the bow wave like they have tickets.
Gullrock rises out of the haze: a hunched grey island, cliffs on three sides, and on the highest point a red-and-white lighthouse like a stick of rock somebody forgot to eat.
Pony is at the rail with the passport open, reading the riddle again under his breath.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "Climb to the keeper, who never sleeps, and ask her the hour the ocean keeps."

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Tide table.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Tide table. But it's not just "go to the lighthouse". The stamp's somewhere you can only reach at a certain tide.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: She wants us to read the hour, *then* go.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Pia's riddles have homework.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Pia's riddles have layers. Like a trifle.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Or a sunburn.
He touches his nose without thinking. It's peeling at the tip. Clover's aloe did heroic work overnight, but there's only so much a rabbit can fix.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You were never going to let that go, were you.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Never.
Further down the rail, Fenn stands alone, hood up, hands in pockets, watching the island come closer like a chessboard.
Clover is talking to the captain about his dog. The dog has decided Clover is the best thing that's happened to it all year.
Zizzy looks down at the bow cutting a clean white line through the silver.
Her grandmother was afraid of boats. She went on them anyway, every summer.
Zizzy doesn't know why that's come back today. It sits beside her at the rail, quiet and heavy, like a second passenger.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You've gone somewhere again.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Ferry times.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: We're on the ferry.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The next ferry.
He moves along the rail a little, until his elbow is nearly touching hers, and stays there.
The road up to the lighthouse is short and brutal. Halfway, they get off and push. At the top, the wind hits like a slammed door.
Close up, the red stripes have faded to the pink of old brick.
At the base: a brass plaque and, in a glass-fronted case, a tide table printed on yellowed card.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Low water today: 4:52 p.m. High water: 10:58 a.m. and 11:13 p.m.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: "The hour the ocean keeps." Keeps. As in holds onto. High tide.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Or as in "keeps back." Low tide. When the sea gives something up.
They look at each other. Then they both look at the brass plaque.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "Gullrock Light, 1862. Built after the wreck of the *Constance*,

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: whose bell may still be seen at the lowest tides beneath Keeper's Point."
A beat.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The bell can be *seen*. At the lowest tides.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: 4:52. The stamp's at the bell.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's ten past nine.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: We've got seven hours and forty minutes to kill on an island that's mostly rock.
Behind them, a quiet voice.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Most people go down at eleven. High tide. Think the hour means "keeps."
He's on the low wall by the lighthouse door, hood down, copper hair blown everywhere, eating an apple. He doesn't look at them.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: And you?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Sat here two years ago from nine till five. Didn't move. Clover hated it.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I did hate it! I counted three hundred and twelve seagulls.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I named eleven of them.
She flops down beside Fenn, beaming at Zizzy as if they've known each other for years.

steps.speaker: clover
