else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: Don't.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: — a bump.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: …We didn't call it.

steps.text: — and the door of the hut crashes open.
Wind and rain roar in. The lamp swings wildly. Fifteen sleeping cyclists wake up shouting.
In the doorway, streaming water: a rabbit in a soaked olive trench coat, ears plastered flat, and a fox with his hood up and his arm round her.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Sorry! Sorry, sorry — is there room?

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: We'd made it to the jetty, we thought we'd beaten it, and then the jetty *flooded*, and the ferry's not coming, and we had to come *back* —

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Shut the door.
Somebody shuts the door. Fenn steers Clover to the only space left, directly in front of Zizzy and Pony, folds himself down beside her, and looks up.
He stamps their passport at the box by the door without looking, as if he knew it would be there.
Then he looks at Zizzy. At Pony. At the gap between them, which is now a very careful, very obvious six inches.
He doesn't say anything. One eyebrow goes up a millimetre, and down again.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Oh — oh, did we interrupt —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: No.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: No!

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Oh, we *totally* did.
The tide turns at a quarter past eight, as the otters promised. By nine the storm has blown out to a grumble and a drizzle.
The causeway is a road again, gleaming wet under a torn, moonlit sky.
The tandem has a snapped chain, a bent rear mudguard and a slow puncture. Zizzy fixes the puncture by lamplight while the otters hold the torch. The chain she can't fix. Not here.
So they walk: the whole hut, wheeling their bikes on across the bottom of the sea by moonlight, towards the Spit.
The flats shine silver either side. Somewhere out in the dark, the sea is pretending nothing happened.
At the far end, Bruno's van waits with its headlights on and, for once, the saxophone off.
Fenn and Clover walk ahead. Clover leans on Fenn a little. She twisted her left ankle on the hut ladder, scrambling up out of the flood. Giraffy will strap it tomorrow.
Fenn carries both their bikes, one in each hand, without comment.
Pony walks beside Zizzy, pushing the broken tandem.

then.text: He's still wearing the coat. He hasn't offered it back. She hasn't asked.
She hasn't said a word since the hut. He keeps glancing at her. Finally:

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Did I say something wrong? About the teacher?

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: No.
She wants to say: the board by the window is fourteen Mill Street. It still squeaks. I've re-screwed it four times since spring.
The woman in the purple coat was my grandmother. And she's gone.
But if she says it, it's real. Him at nine, by the window she grew up beside. The two of them, ten years apart, on the same floor.
It's too big. She can't hold it yet, not on a causeway in the dark with her legs shaking.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Not yet. Ask me again. Later.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I'll tell you something. Not yet.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Okay. Later.

steps.text: Halfway across, he bumps her shoulder with his. Like the tandem going over a crack in the road.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Bump.
She doesn't look at him. But she bumps back.
Bruno has the van's back doors open, a camping stove going and a pan of something hot.
He doesn't make a single joke as the cyclists stagger in off the causeway. That's how everyone knows it was bad.
He hands Zizzy a mug. Looks at the tandem, the snapped chain. Exhales slowly.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Sit down, sunshine. Both of you. I'll look at it in the morning.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Can you fix it?

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Don't know. Frame took a knock. We'll see when it's light.
Then his gaze slides to Pony, standing beside her in the dark.

then.text: In a purple coat that is clearly hers, two sizes too small for him.
Bruno's face does something sly and delighted, and underneath, for one second, very soft.

then.speaker: bruno
then.text: Oh, strawberry.

else.text: And Bruno's face does something soft for one second, before it remembers itself.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Bed. The Spit campsite's up the hill. Your tent's pitched. Don't ask me how.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: I'm a hero. Nobody appreciates me.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I appreciate you.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: …I know you do, mate. That's the problem.

chapters.title: Fenn's Offer
chapters.subtitle: Day 7 (Friday), the Spit, then Hallow Key.

steps.text: The morning after a storm is always unreasonably beautiful.
The Spit campsite sits on a grassy hump above the jetty. Below it, the world has been rinsed: hard blue sky, mud flats shining silver, the causeway a black thread stitched back towards Sorrel.
Washing lines have sprung up between the tents, sagging with wet kit.
Zizzy is at the van by half past six. Bruno is already under the tandem, which lies upside down on a tarp like a beetle on its back.
He says nothing for a long time. Then he slides out, sits up, and wipes his hands on a rag.
His face is serious. In seven days she's learned that a serious Bruno is more frightening than any storm.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Chain's easy. I've got a spare. Mudguard, easy. The rear stay's cracked. Here.
He runs a greasy fingertip along the thin tube by the back wheel. A hairline split in the metal, no longer than a fingernail.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: I can splint it. Hose clamps, a bit of tube, some swearing. It'll hold on the flat. Hallow Key's flat.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: But Lastlight's the climb. Two riders standing on the pedals up that hill, pulling hard —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It'll break.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: It might. Might not. I'm a mechanic, not a fortune teller.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: If I were you, I'd take the climb steady and pray to whatever you pray to.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I don't pray.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Then shout at it. Works for me.
He lays out tools. Hose clamps. A length of old inner tube. The dead man's spanners. Then, without looking up:

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Nice coat he was wearing last night.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: …It was cold.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Mm. It was. Freezing.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Otters were saying something about a bit of a moment in the hut. Before the rabbit came in.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The otters are liars.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Otters are famously honest. It's why nobody likes them.
She turns to go. Behind her, Bruno speaks in a different voice, lower. The voice he keeps for the dead man's spanners.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Hey. Sunshine.
She stops.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Whatever you're carrying. You don't have to carry it on the bike's cracked bits. That's all.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: That's my one wise thing for the year. Don't tell anyone.
She doesn't know how to answer. She walks up the hill with her arms folded. He goes back to swearing at a hose clamp.

then.text: Pony sits on the grass outside tent forty-one with the purple coat folded very neatly on his knees, like something on loan from a museum, and the riddle card from the hut in his hand.

else.text: Pony sits on the grass outside tent forty-one, his beanie drying on a tent peg, the riddle card from the hut in his hand.

steps.text: He looks up when she comes back. His face does what it's started doing every time it sees her: a small, quick brightening, like a lamp turned up.
She's been noticing it for days. She doesn't know what to do with it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Riddle six. It was in the stamp box, under the ink pad.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I only found it this morning.
In Pia's bold, looping hand:
*"Where the roof fell in and the prayers flew out, where the walls still stand though the saints have left — at the end of the day, when the sky catches fire, look up, and you'll find what's kept."*

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: "Roof fell in." A ruin.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Hallow Key has a ruined chapel. St Brannoc's. Twelfth century. The roof fell in during a storm in 1703.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: "When the sky catches fire": the fireworks. Tomorrow night's the festival.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: The stamp's in the chapel, but you can only find it at sunset, when the light comes through the arches. I think.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You think.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I think very confidently.
She sits beside him on the damp grass. Their shoulders don't touch.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You said "later." In the dark. About the teacher.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I know.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Is it later yet?

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Not yet. Soon. I promise.
He nods. He trusts the promise, plain as print, and it nearly undoes her.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: About last night —

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The bike's cracked.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: The rear stay. Bruno's splinting it. It'll hold on the flat. Maybe not on the climb.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: That's what matters. That's what we need to talk about.
He looks at her for a long moment. Then he lets the other thing go — she watches him set it down, carefully, like the coat — and nods.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Okay. The bike.
She hates herself a little. Just enough.
The ferry to Hallow Key leaves the Spit jetty at two. Most teams spend the morning drying kit and limping about.
Clover's ankle is in a bandage Giraffy tied with great care. She hops round the campsite insisting it's "barely a sprain", wincing whenever she thinks nobody's looking.
At eleven, Zizzy walks down alone to check the ferry board. Fenn is there, on a bollard at the end of the pier, hood down, hands in pockets, looking out at the flats.
He doesn't turn round. He just says:

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Sit, if you want.
She doesn't sit. She leans on the rail a few feet away. Gulls. Water slapping the pilings. The causeway steaming faintly in the sun.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Bruno told me about your frame.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Bruno tells everyone everything.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Not everything. Just the useful bits.
Another silence. He's better at those than she is.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Clover's ankle's worse than she says. She can ride.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: She can't climb. Not Lastlight. Not fast.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Why are you telling me?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Because I'm going to ask you something, and you should know why.
He takes a folded, laminated card out of his pocket and holds it out without looking at her.
A page of the race rules. One paragraph underlined, neatly, in pencil.

*Rule 14. Should a team be unable to continue together, a rider may join another team at the Hallow Key checkpoint, with the consent of all riders. A team of three may cross the line together and share the prize as they agree. The rider left behind may not finish. — P.*
She reads it twice. The last sentence three times.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Your bike's going to break on the climb. Ours is fine, but Clover can't push it.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Your silver bike's in Bruno's van. Ride it with us from Hallow Key. You're faster than me on climbs.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You pace, Clover sits on your wheel all the way up. We win.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: And the money.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You take my half. Four thousand. Clover keeps hers.
She turns and stares at him.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You'd give me your half.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: I don't need it.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Then what do you need?
He's quiet for a long time.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Three. Three wins. Nobody's done three.
He says it to the flats, not to her. Plain, like he's reading it off a plaque that isn't there yet.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Without it I'm just a guy who used to be good at a bike race.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: I don't — I don't really have a second thing.
The most words she's heard him say in a row. Also the most honest. She almost wishes they weren't.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: And Pony?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.expr_raw: not looking away from the flats
steps.text: Can't finish without a partner. That's the rule.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: He needs to *finish* this. You can see it on him. Every day, every mile. He's never —
She stops. That's Pony's story. It isn't hers to tell Fenn.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: I know. I've watched him all week. He's good.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: He'd be fine. He'd be sad. He'd be fine.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You don't know that.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: No.

then.text: He turns his head, slightly, and looks at her for the first time.

then.speaker: fenn
then.text: I said you owed me one. On the heath. This is the one.
It lands like a hand on her arm. Not hard. Just there.

steps.text: She looks down at the card. At *the rider left behind may not finish*.
Four thousand. Fourteen Mill Street. The floor, the mirror, the board by the window. All of it saved, on a silver bike with two near-strangers.
And a horse in a beanie at a finish line he'll never cross, holding a broken tandem with a duck on it.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I need the money. There's a — lease. A place.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: If I don't pay by September, it's gone.
She didn't mean to tell him. Things keep coming out of her this week, as if the storm loosened a board.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Then you know what it's worth.
He stands. Both hands back in his pockets.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Tell me by tonight. On the ferry, or at the Hallow Key checkpoint.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You don't have to tell him till you're sure. Your call.
He walks off down the jetty. A few steps on, he stops, and adds without turning:

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: For what it's worth, I'd rather race you. Properly. Both teams, all the way up.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: That'd be better.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: But I'd rather win than lose.
He goes. Zizzy stands on the jetty holding the card for a long time.
Ten minutes later Clover hops up the jetty on her bandaged ankle, red-faced, out of breath, ears flat.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: He asked you. Didn't he. Rule fourteen. He asked you.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You knew?

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I found the card in his hoodie this morning. I *told* him not to. I told him I'm fine, I can climb, we can do it, the two of us.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: And he just said "Clover", like that, in that voice. Like I'm a nice idea that won't work.
Her ears have drooped to her shoulders. Zizzy has never seen her without the sunshine. It's like watching a field go grey under a cloud.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I don't want to win like that. I want to win *with* him. Just once. Me and him.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Not him and some better rider he picked up at a checkpoint.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: And I don't want to win by leaving Pony at the side of the road with a broken bike. That's not a race. That's just — taking.
She wipes her eyes with the back of her hand, furious with herself.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Sorry. I'm not angry at you. You haven't done anything.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: Have you?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Not yet.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: But you're thinking about it.
Zizzy doesn't answer. She doesn't need to. Clover listens with her whole body.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I'd think about it too, if I needed something that much. I won't hate you, whatever you pick.

steps.speaker: clover
steps.text: I just want you to know what it costs. Not just him. You.
She squeezes Zizzy's arm once, very hard, and hops away.
The ferry to Hallow Key is crowded, noisy and bright with afternoon sun. Riders compare storm stories, which have already grown by about forty per cent.
The tandem is lashed to the deck rail, splinted at the back with hose clamps and black inner tube. It looks like it's been to war. The duck bell survived.
Pony sits on a coil of rope beside it, absorbed in a leaflet about St Brannoc's. Now and then he reads her a line. She doesn't hear any of them.
Ten minutes out, Pony disappears into the ferry's tiny galley and comes back with one paper cone of chips: steaming, salted, drowning in vinegar, a little wooden fork stuck in the top.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: They only had one size. "Enormous."

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I think it's for two. Possibly four.
He holds it out at the rail between them. She means to say no. Her stomach says something else, loudly. He politely pretends not to hear.
They eat at the rail, wind in their faces. One wooden fork, passed back and forth, then abandoned for fingers.
The vinegar stings the scrapes on his knuckles. He winces and keeps eating.
She picks out the crispy end bits and puts them, one by one, on his side of the cone, without looking at him.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Those are the best bits.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I don't like them.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Everyone likes them.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Eat the chips, Pony.
A gull hangs above them, matching the ferry's speed, wings perfectly still, eyeing the cone.
Pony holds one long chip up to it, very solemnly, like a knight offering a sword.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Don't.
The gull takes it with surgical precision and peels away. Pony stares at his empty fingers.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: It didn't even touch me.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Professional.
For three minutes, salt on her fingers and sun on the water, she forgets the card in her pocket entirely.
Then the cone is empty. He folds it into a neat square, the way he folds everything. And she remembers.
Across the deck, Fenn leans on the wheelhouse, hands in pockets, very carefully not looking at her.
Clover sits on the far side with her ankle up, chatting to the otters, laughing too loud.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: — and the legend says if two people see the first firework through the east arch together, they'll — oh.
He stops. Goes pink. Folds the leaflet very small.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: They'll what?

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Nothing. It's a silly legend. Medieval.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: They had a lot of time on their hands.
She looks at him properly. The beanie. The round glasses. The pink rising to the tips of his ears.
The hands on the folded leaflet, still scraped raw from dragging the tandem up the ladder. The face that brightens every time it sees her.
She thinks about the finish at Lastlight. Him beside it with a broken bike, watching her cross on a silver one with somebody else.
She thinks about the floor at fourteen Mill Street. Sold. Flats with pale grey carpets, and nobody saying "*again*".
She thinks about her grandmother: *That isn't strength, chérie. It's just being lonely on purpose.*
And she thinks, very clearly, the coldest thought of the week: *He'd be sad. He'd be fine.*
Across the deck, Fenn looks up. Meets her eyes. Waits.

options.label: Refuse. Walk over and say it to his face: "No. We're finishing together."

steps.text: She crosses the deck. Fenn straightens against the wheelhouse.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: No.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: No?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: No. We're finishing together. On that.
She jerks her chin at the tandem, splinted and scarred, with its duck.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: If it breaks on the climb, we push it.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: We pushed it through a flood. We can push it up a hill.
Fenn looks at the tandem. At Pony, still pink, unfolding the leaflet. Back at her.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Okay.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: That's it? "Okay"?

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Asked. You answered. It's a good answer.
He looks across at Clover, ankle up on a crate.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: She's going to kill me.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: She's going to forgive you. That's worse.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: Yeah.
She goes back and sits on the rope coil beside Pony, closer than she needs to. He looks up, surprised.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: What did Fenn want?

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: To buy me. He offered me his half of the prize if I left you at Hallow Key and rode with them.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Rule fourteen.
Pony goes very still.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I said no.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: But the salle —

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: We'll win it. Or we won't. Together. That's the plan.
He stares at her for a long moment. Then he looks down at the leaflet and says nothing, and she can't read his face at all.
She'll find out tomorrow what he was thinking.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: Nothing. Race stuff.
He nods. He believes her. She tells herself it's true.

options.label: "I'll think about it." Buy time.

steps.text: She doesn't cross the deck. She holds Fenn's gaze and tilts her head, very slightly. Not yes. Not no.
*Later.*
He nods once, and looks away.
Beside her, Pony goes back to the twelfth-century masonry of St Brannoc's. She sits down next to him and doesn't hear a word.
The card stays in her pocket, warm as a coal.

options.label: Nod. Accept in secret. Don't tell Pony.

steps.text: She holds Fenn's gaze for a long time. Then, very slightly, she nods.
Just once.
He doesn't smile. He looks at her a moment longer, as if checking she meant it, then turns to the sea.
Pony looks up from the leaflet and smiles at her, that quick brightening. "Did you know they found a medieval coin in the font?"
"No," she says, and smiles back.
It's the hardest thing she's ever done with her face.
She sits beside him on the rope. Their shoulders touch. He leans in, just slightly, trusting.
She lets him. She tells herself it's kind.
Hallow Key is the busiest island yet: a harbour town of crooked painted houses climbing a hill, every one hung with lanterns and flags for tomorrow's festival.
Stalls are going up in the square. Someone is testing a sound system with the same three seconds of an old pop song, over and over. The air smells of frying doughnuts and gunpowder.
Giraffy is at the checkpoint on the harbour wall under his parasol, calmly checking in each team. He looks at the splinted tandem for a long moment.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: It came through.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Mostly.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Mostly's how most things come through.
No stamp here. Just a tick on his clipboard: this is Rule 14's checkpoint. Zizzy sees him glance from her to Fenn, a little way off, and back.
He says nothing. He ticks forty-one, then, very gently, puts one long hand on Pony's beanie, the way he did in the orchard.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Get some sleep. Tomorrow's long. Then the day after's longer.
On her way up to the campsite, Zizzy passes the harbour office. Pia is pinning tomorrow's festival notices to the board, one drawing pin in each corner, all exactly level.
Pia sees her and freezes, pin in hand, like someone caught somewhere she shouldn't be.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Forty-one. You came through the storm.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You put the stamp in the hut.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: I always do. Just in case.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: People should be — rewarded. For getting in out of the rain.
She looks at Zizzy, at the bedraggled feather, for longer than is comfortable. Behind the enormous glasses her eyes are suddenly bright.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: You look like someone I used to know. When you stand like that.

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Feet like that.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: Like what?

steps.speaker: pia
steps.text: Nothing. Sorry. It's — I'm tired. Storms. Sorry. Good night.
She goes in and shuts the door. Through the window Zizzy sees her sit at a desk, take off her glasses, and put her face in her hands.
Then the glasses go back on, and she picks up a pen and writes, fast and bold, the way she writes riddles.
Zizzy stands outside a moment longer, feet still planted in the old French stance — front foot forward, back foot square — that her grandmother drilled into her before she could read.
She hadn't noticed. She never does. It's just how she stands.
The campsite is a terraced field above the town, looking down over the rooftops to the harbour. Tent forty-one, as always, is the smallest, last in the row.
That night she lies listening to the sound system three fields away playing its three seconds of song, to Pony breathing through the divider, and to the sea.

then.text: She doesn't sleep. She lies with Rule 14 in one hand and the ammonite in the other, trying to work out which is heavier.
Through the divider, half asleep, he whispers: "Night, Zizzy. Big day tomorrow. Fireworks."
She can't answer. She presses the back of her hand to her mouth and lies very still.
She doesn't sleep much. The card is in her pannier. She keeps thinking she hears it rustle.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Night, Zizzy. Fireworks tomorrow.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: …Night.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: Zizzy? Thank you. For whatever you said to Fenn.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: You had the "up" face, and then you didn't.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: You were watching?

else.speaker: pony
else.text: I'm always watching your shoulders. For steering.
She smiles into the dark. Bruno would never let her live it down.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: Goodnight, Pony.

steps.text: Festival morning on Hallow Key starts at nine with the brass band — still following the race "for the cider", now visibly sunburned — marching through the square playing something triumphant and slightly wrong.
The square is transformed. Stalls in every colour: doughnuts, crab sandwiches, glass floats, knitted things, a man selling only hats.
Lanterns strung between the crooked houses. A stage at one end. Children everywhere. Dogs everywhere. One goat, unexplained.
The race has the day off till sunset. The stamp at St Brannoc's can only be found "when the sky catches fire", and everyone agrees that means evening.
So forty teams of sunburned, storm-battered cyclists wander the festival like sailors on shore leave.
Pony is quiet.
That's the first thing Zizzy notices. He reads the signs as always — HOMEMADE FUDGE, CRAB (FRESH), CRAB (LESS FRESH, CHEAPER) — but silently.
He doesn't read her a single plaque all morning. When she hands him a doughnut, he says "thank you" and eats it slowly, looking at the harbour.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You're not talking.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Hm? I'm talking.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You haven't told me a fact in two hours. I've started to miss them.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: It's disturbing.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Hallow Key exports four hundred tonnes of crab a year.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: That's a fact with no heart in it.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Sorry. I'm just — thinking.
She waits for him to say what about. He doesn't. He looks at the harbour.
He folds the doughnut paper into a small neat square and puts it in his pocket. She's never seen him keep rubbish before.
Giraffy has a doughnut stall, of course. He fries them one at a time with total serenity while a queue of thirty children vibrates in front of him.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: It'll be ready when it's ready. That's what makes it good.

steps.speaker: extra
steps.name: Child
steps.text: But I want it *now*.

steps.speaker: giraffy
steps.text: Everybody does. That's why it's worth waiting for.
Bruno leans on the next stall, eating Giraffy's doughnuts without paying and needling everyone who passes.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Forty-one! The heroes of the causeway!

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Strawberry, you've got sugar on your nose. No, other side. No — leave it. It's a good look.
Pony wipes his nose without looking. He doesn't laugh. Bruno's eyes narrow, very slightly, and flick to Zizzy.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.expr_raw: low, to her, as Pony wanders off to look at glass floats
steps.text: What's up with him?

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: Hm. One of you's carrying something. I can always tell.

steps.speaker: bruno
steps.text: You walk like the frame's cracked.
Across the square, Clover sits on the edge of the fountain with her bandaged ankle up. Fenn is beside her. They're not talking.
As Zizzy watches, Fenn takes one hand out of his hoodie pocket and puts it, awkwardly, on top of Clover's on the stone rim. And leaves it there.
Clover looks down at it. Her ears come up slowly, like flowers after rain.
St Brannoc's stands on a headland at the edge of town: four roofless walls of honey-coloured stone, tall pointed arches open to the sky, ivy pouring down the inside like green water.
Grass where the floor used to be. Swallows nesting in the empty window frames.
At seven, as the sun drops towards the sea, the whole field stands about in the grass, looking up at the arches, waiting for the sky to catch fire.
Then it does. The sun touches the horizon and the light goes gold, orange, deep red.
It pours through the west arch in a long beam across the chapel and lands, like a pointing finger, on one carved stone high on the east wall, beside the east arch. A little carved bird.
In a niche behind the bird, just out of reach, something glints.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.expr_raw: breathless, back to himself for a second
steps.text: There. *There*. Look up and find what's kept.
The niche is three metres up. Fenn, nearest, looks at it, then turns to Pony.

steps.speaker: fenn
steps.text: You're taller than Clover. I'll lift.
Fenn makes a step of his hands. Pony climbs, wobbling, steadied by Zizzy's hand on his back, and reaches into the niche.
He comes down with a rubber stamp shaped like a bird and a stack of sealed cream envelopes, each with a team number in Pia's bold hand.
He hands Fenn theirs. He stamps both passports. Six. One to go.
Envelope forty-one says, on the back: *The last riddle. Do not open until morning. — P.*

The other teams surge forward for their envelopes. In the crush, with the red light fading and the first lanterns coming on in town, Pony and Zizzy end up alone by the east arch, under the carved bird.
Pony turns to her. His face isn't brightening. It's set, like at the chalk line.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: Zizzy. I need to talk to you.

then.text: He holds out a sheet from Giraffy's clipboard: the Hallow Key checkpoint list.
Next to forty-one, in Giraffy's careful hand: *Rule 14 — Z. to join Team 7 at Lastlight start (pending). Partner informed: ?*

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Giraffy didn't show me. It blew off the clipboard.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I picked it up for him.
He's looking at the question mark.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: "Partner informed." Question mark.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Were you going to tell me? Before tomorrow? Or were you just going to — go?

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I was going to tell you.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: When? At the start line? "Bye, Pony, thanks for the ammonite"?

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Don't. You don't know what it's for. You don't know what I —

then.speaker: pony
then.text: No! I don't! Because you stopped telling me!

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You told me about the salle. By the stream. I thought that meant we were — and then you made a deal behind my back anyway.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: No! I don't! Because you never *tell* me anything!

else.speaker: pony
else.text: Eight days! I told you about the swimming, and the degree, and the washing line, and my *sister*.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: And you went and made a deal with *Fenn*. Whatever it's for, you could tell him. You couldn't tell me.

then.text: That lands. She sees it land on both of them.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I thought we were a team. I thought I was finally finishing something with someone.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: And I'm just the thing you put down when something better came along. Like everyone puts me down. Like I put everything down.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: That's not fair.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: No. It's not.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Fenn said something. Just now, while he was lifting me.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: "Hope she gets her lease sorted. Whatever happens tomorrow." Like I'd know what he meant.
Zizzy goes cold.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Fourteen Mill Street. That's it, isn't it. The postcard with nobody to send it to. The letter you read in the meadow.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You need the money for something real. Something huge. And you told *Fenn*. You told Fenn and not me.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: And he said "whatever happens tomorrow".

then.speaker: pony
then.text: He offered you something. Didn't he. And you didn't say no.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I didn't say yes.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You didn't say no.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: It wasn't yours to know.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You keep *saying* that! Everything's "not mine". I've sat behind you on a bicycle for eight days!

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I know when you're about to change gear before you do. I know you count in French and you hate fêtes and you sleep with that stone in your hand.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I *know* you. And you won't let me know anything that *matters*.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Because then you'd look at me like — like *that*. Like you're looking now.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I'm looking at you like someone who'd have helped. That's all this face is.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You just never let me.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: I talked to Fenn this afternoon.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: About what?

else.speaker: pony
else.text: About rule fourteen. I asked if the offer was still open. He said yes.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: So I'm withdrawing. Tomorrow morning. I'll tell Pia.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: You ride with Fenn and Clover on your silver bike. You win. You get four thousand. You save the salle.
For a second she can't speak at all.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: The bike's going to break on that climb. Bruno said so. Then we both lose, and you lose *everything*. The floor and the mirror and the board by the window.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: And I'd just lose a bike race. I've lost loads of things. I'm really good at it. It's the one thing I'm qualified for.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: You *decided*.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: What?

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: You went to Fenn. Behind my back. And decided what I could carry.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: You decided I couldn't carry losing, so you'd carry it for me. Without asking.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: I was trying to *help* —

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: That's what *I* do! That's the thing I do, the thing she told me not to do, my whole life — and you're doing it to *me*.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: You came here to *finish* something, Pony. And you're quitting it. For *me*.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: Do you know how that feels? Do you have any idea?

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You were going to say yes. On the ferry. I saw your face.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: You told me you said no, but you were thinking about it.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I was *thinking*. Thinking isn't deciding.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: *You* decided.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: I thought it was what you wanted.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: Then you weren't watching my shoulders.

steps.text: The silence afterwards is enormous. Down in town the band has started up again.
In the empty window above them, a swallow shifts in its nest.
Pony steps back. His face has gone very still and very young, the way it looked without his glasses on the verge.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: I'm going to go and — walk. For a bit. I'm sorry.
He walks out through the east arch, down the headland path towards the harbour, into the dusk and the lanterns and the crowds. The beanie is the last thing she can see.

steps.prompt: He's walking away. The fireworks start in twenty minutes.

options.label: Go after him. Now.

steps.text: She stands there for three seconds. *Un. Deux. Trois.* So nothing she does next is done in a temper.
Then she runs.
Down the headland path in the dusk, hat ribbon flying, through the crowds at the edge of town.
Past the doughnut stall, where Giraffy raises a calm hand and points, without a word, to the harbour wall.
Along the quay, dodging children with sparklers, until she sees him.
He's at the end of the harbour wall, legs over the dark water, the wooden sword across his knees.

options.label: Wait here, under the east arch. If he comes back, he comes back.

steps.text: She doesn't run after him. She sits on a fallen stone under the east arch, under the carved bird, hands clasped between her knees.
She waits. It's harder than the causeway.
Every part of her wants to get up and do something. Fix something. Lunge.
She waits anyway. Her grandmother's voice: *Sometimes the bout is just standing still, chérie, and letting them come to you.*
Twelve minutes. Thirteen. The light's nearly gone. Lanterns bob down in the harbour.
The swallow drops out of the window frame, circles the nave once, and goes back in. She envies it.
Then footsteps on the path. A beanie in the dark. He comes back through the east arch and stops when he sees her.

steps.speaker: pony
steps.text: You waited.

steps.speaker: zizzy
steps.text: You came back.

options.label: Let him go.

steps.text: She lets him go.
She stands under the east arch and watches the beanie disappear into the crowds, and doesn't move.
Moving would mean admitting she wants to. She's spent eight days, and a whole life, not admitting what she wants.
When she finally walks down into town, alone, the fireworks are about to start.

then.text: She stops a few feet away. Out of breath. Hat askew.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: You don't get to quit this.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Zizzy —

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: No. My turn. You let me finish first.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: That's the rule. Your rule.
He goes still. Then, slowly, he nods.

else.text: He stays in the arch. She stays on the stone. Between them, the grass and the last of the light.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: Can I say something? You can tell me I'm wrong after.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: But you have to let me finish first.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: That's my rule.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: I'm borrowing it.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: You were right. I decide what people can carry. I always decide they can't.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: My grandmother told me it was being lonely on purpose. I didn't listen, and then she was gone.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Then you got on the back of my bike and started carrying things anyway. Without asking.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: It's the first time in five months I haven't felt like I was holding everything up on my own.
Her voice wobbles. She lets it.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: So I was furious. Because you did the thing I do, and I finally saw it from the other side.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: It looks like someone you — someone you care about, disappearing so you don't have to see them hurt.
Pony is staring at her.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I don't want the salle without you. I don't want four thousand pounds if you're at the bottom of the hill with a broken bike.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I want to push the stupid tandem up that hill with you. If it breaks, we carry it. Together.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: That's the plan.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Whose plan?

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Ours. It's new.
Out over the harbour: a thump, a hiss, a long rising whistle.
And the first firework of the Hallow Key festival bursts over the sea.
Gold. Enormous. Framed perfectly in the east arch of St Brannoc's, where two people are standing together.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: The legend —

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: I read the leaflet. While I was waiting.

else.text: Gold. Enormous. Reflected in the dark water below, so it bursts twice: once in the sky, once at their feet.

then.text: Pony stands up from the harbour wall.

else.text: Pony steps forward out of the arch.

then.text: The sword is in one hand. He puts it down on the stone, carefully, the way he does with the things that matter.
He takes off his glasses. Folds them. Puts them on top of the sword.
She takes off the hat.
Neither of them says "up". Neither needs to.
They lean in at exactly the same moment, the way they rose together over the first pothole on the heath, without counting, without being told.
The kiss is soft and a little clumsy, and tastes of doughnut sugar and salt.
It goes on through three fireworks: gold, then green, then a shower of white that falls slowly, like snow in August.
When they break apart, his forehead stays against hers. He's laughing, very quietly, breathless.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I've wanted to do that since the sunscreen.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: The *sunscreen*?

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Maybe the bunting.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: You were tied up in bunting.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I was very sure of my feelings in the bunting.
She kisses him again to stop him talking. It doesn't work. He's smiling too much. It doesn't matter.
All of Hallow Key is looking at the sky. Nobody is looking at them.
Except, far off on the fountain's rim, a rabbit with her ears straight up and her paws pressed to her mouth, and a fox beside her who, for once, is visibly smiling.
And near a doughnut stall, a giraffe nods once, as if confirming something he's known for a week, and turns the next doughnut.
Much later, when the last firework has faded and the band has finally, mercifully, run out of cider, they walk back up through the town to the campsite above the harbour.
Hand in hand. Not talking.
Tent forty-one. Smallest. Last in the row. Down in the town, the lanterns are going out one by one.
Pony stops outside it. Looks at the tent. Looks at her.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: The divider —

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Whose rule was that?

then.speaker: pony
then.text: …Yours.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Then I'll decide.
She unzips the tent and holds out her hand.
The campsite wakes at dawn to three long, rude blasts of Bruno's van horn, and Bruno bellowing across the terraces:

then.speaker: bruno
then.text: RISE AND SHINE, WAYFARERS! LAST DAY! FERRY TO LASTLIGHT AT NINE!

then.speaker: bruno
then.text: AND WHOEVER'S IN TENT FORTY-ONE — I KNOW. I *KNOW*.
Inside the tent, the divider is rolled up neatly in the corner. A beanie and a purple hat lie side by side by the door.
Two people are laughing into each other's shoulders, trying very hard not to make a sound.
On the groundsheet between them lies a cream envelope. *The last riddle. Do not open until morning.*
It's morning.

then.text: She stops a few feet away. He doesn't turn round.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Pony.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I need a bit, Zizzy. Please. Just — a bit.
She wants to say everything. She doesn't know how. It's stuck under the armour, under eight days and five months and a whole life of not saying it.
So she sits on the harbour wall. Not beside him. A metre away. Close enough that he knows she's there. Far enough that he doesn't have to look at her.
He stands in the arch. She sits on the stone. Neither knows what to say.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: I came back for the bike. Bruno said not to leave it in the chapel overnight.
It isn't true. They both know. It's all either of them can manage.

else.text: She finds a space at the back of the crowd on the quay. Alone. Hat low.

then.text: The first firework goes up over the harbour with a thump and a whistle and bursts gold across the sky.
Everyone in Hallow Key looks up. A thousand faces lit gold, then green, then white.
Children shrieking. The band playing along, badly. Somewhere, a dog howling at the sky.
Across the quay, through the crowd, she sees him: on the harbour wall, beanie, sword across his knees, face turned up to the light. Alone too.
Between them: a hundred people, the noise, eight days, and everything neither of them said.
He doesn't see her. Or he does, and looks away. She can't tell from here.
She's spent a week learning to read his shoulders. From here, she can't see them.

else.text: They watch the whole thing a metre apart. Gold, green, a long slow shower of white like snow in August.
She glances at him once. He's watching the sky. His face is wet, and he doesn't wipe it.
She doesn't reach for his hand. She wants to so badly it's like a cramp. She doesn't.

then.text: Across the quay, on the fountain's rim, Clover leans against Fenn's shoulder, and Fenn has his arm round her. They look happy. Zizzy is glad for them. She's surprised how glad.
And how much it hurts.
They walk back up to the campsite separately, ten minutes apart. Tent forty-one. Smallest. Last in the row.
The divider stays zipped.
She lies in the dark listening to him not sleeping on the other side of it. The ammonite in one hand. The sealed envelope in the other. *Do not open until morning.*
In her pannier, Rule 14 is still folded. Fenn hasn't said anything. Neither has she.
Tomorrow at the start line, in front of everyone, she'll have to choose which bike to get on.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Zizzy?
She holds her breath.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: …Never mind. Goodnight.
She doesn't answer. She lies awake until the sky goes grey.
At dawn, Pia's handbell rings down the rows of tents, small and polite and insistent, like Pia.

then.speaker: pia
then.text: Morning. Sorry. Morning. Last day. Ferry at nine. Sorry.
Zizzy sits up. On the other side of the divider, Pony sits up too.
Neither of them says good morning.
The envelope is in her hand. *The last riddle.*
It's morning.
Bruno's horn is still echoing off the terraces when a second voice comes: calm, unhurried, carrying easily from two metres up.

then.speaker: giraffy
then.text: Chapel steps, thirty minutes. Pia's last riddle. Chapel steps, thirty minutes.
Inside tent forty-one, Pony has his face pressed into Zizzy's shoulder, shaking with silent laughter.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: He *knows*.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Bruno knew on day one. He's just been waiting for an excuse to use the horn.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Everyone's going to look at us.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Let them.
She says it so simply that he stops laughing and just looks at her.
Then he finds his glasses and his beanie, puts both on with enormous dignity, and gets the beanie on backwards.
She turns it round for him. Her hand stays on his cheek a second longer.

else.text: Pia's handbell is still tinkling down the rows when a second voice comes: calm, unhurried, carrying easily from two metres up.

else.speaker: giraffy
else.text: Chapel steps, thirty minutes. Pia's last riddle. Chapel steps, thirty minutes.
Inside tent forty-one, two people sit on opposite sides of a zipped nylon divider and listen to each other not saying anything.
Zizzy dresses in the grey light. Purple shirt. Hat. The envelope goes in her pocket next to the ammonite.
When she unzips the tent, Pony is already on the grass outside, boots on, sword across his knees, looking down at the harbour.
He looks round. His face starts to brighten, out of habit, then remembers and stops. That's worse than if it hadn't moved at all.

else.speaker: pony
else.text: Morning.

else.speaker: zizzy
else.text: Morning.

steps.text: Thirty minutes is too long to stand about and too short to do anything useful. Without discussing it, they walk down through the waking town to the harbour wall.
The festival is a wreck of itself at dawn: bunting sagging, paper cups in the gutters, one spent sparkler on the cobbles. Someone has left a whole doughnut on a bollard.
The sea is flat and pale pink and absolutely still, as if it's also slightly hungover.
Bruno has left the tandem against the wall where they'll find it: stay freshly re-taped, duck bell polished.
A note is tied to the handlebars: *DON'T STAND ON THE PEDALS ON THE CLIMB. I MEAN IT. — B.* And under it, smaller: *(good luck x)*
They sit on the wall, legs over the water. The envelope lies on the warm stone between them, still sealed.

then.text: She leans against his shoulder. He leans back. For a long time neither says anything, and none of the silence needs filling.
He turns her hand over and traces the thin old scar on her forearm with one fingertip, the way he'd trace a line on a map.

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: Épée. I was twelve. I didn't keep my point down.

then.speaker: pony
then.text: Did she say "again"?

then.speaker: zizzy
then.text: She said "Hospital, then again."
He laughs into her hat brim.
The gap between them is about the width of the gap on the harbour wall last night. Narrower, maybe. It's hard to tell.
A gull lands right in the gap and looks from one to the other, as if waiting to be told which of them to rob.

then.text: Don't. She's had a hard week.
Zizzy looks at him. He isn't looking at her. But he said it.
She tears a corner off the envelope flap, nothing that matters, and holds it out. The gull takes it and leaves. The gap is just stone again.

Pony stares at her for a long time. Then he takes the silver bike from Bruno, who for once says nothing at all, and wheels it to the start.

Ahead, across a strip of bright water, the last island rises: green and steep, one hill climbing out of the sea, and on the very top, small and dark against the sky, the summit cairn.
